iut_type: End Product (Pi Crystal Corporation product using Fanstel BM832 BLE module), reference QDID coverage confirmation via module vendor before registration
customer_question: We want to create a new Product Qualification referencing two specific QDIDs (corresponding to nRF Connect SDK v2.8.0, BLE 5.3 low-level/GAP/GATT/SM) instead of the BM832's currently-referenced older QDID -- can we confirm with the module vendor (Fanstel) that doing so still properly covers our BM832 hardware before we proceed with registration?
question_variants: Does referencing a newer SDK-version QDID require buying a new module variant, or can the same BM832 hardware be used?
Can we also reference a Mesh-capability QDID for this same module under the new SDK version?
actual_issue: The customer wanted to register their product referencing newer QDIDs (tied to nRF Connect SDK v2.8.0) rather than the BM832 module's originally-referenced older QDID, and needed confirmation from the module's actual developer (Fanstel) that this newer reference combination genuinely covered their BM832 hardware before committing to registration on that basis.
plain_english_explanation: The customer proactively emailed the module's chipset/SDK developer (Fanstel) directly with three specific questions: whether the BM832's current QDID reference could be swapped for a different QDID tied to the same Nordic nRF52832 chipset without retesting (confirmed yes -- a Declaration Number can list products with Bluetooth SIG using any compatible QDID for that chipset, no retest required), whether referencing the newer SDK-version QDIDs would allow developing and selling their product using BM832 hardware with that newer SDK (confirmed yes), and whether referencing an additional Mesh-capability QDID under the same SDK version would enable Bluetooth Mesh support on the BM832 (confirmed yes). With this vendor confirmation in hand, the registration proceeded referencing all three QDIDs as planned, with no additional testing required.
consultant_answer: Since you've confirmed directly with Fanstel that the newer QDIDs you want to reference do cover your BM832 hardware (including the Mesh capability reference), we'll proceed with the proxy registration referencing all three QDIDs as planned -- no additional testing needed.
decision_logic: When a customer wants to register a product referencing a different or newer QDID combination than what their module was originally registered under, having the module's actual developer/vendor directly confirm that the new reference combination genuinely covers the hardware is a reliable way to proceed without retesting, since the vendor has authoritative knowledge of what their chipset/SDK combination actually supports.
final_recommendation: When a customer proposes referencing a different QDID combination than their module's original registration, encourage them to get direct written confirmation from the module/chipset vendor that the new combination covers their specific hardware, and proceed with registration on that basis once confirmed, rather than requiring redundant retesting.
risk_if_done_wrong: Proceeding with a new QDID reference combination without vendor confirmation could result in an invalid registration if the referenced QDIDs don't actually cover the customer's specific module hardware.
